\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{حذر} (ḥadhdhara)}{حذر (ḥadhdhara)}]{\ar{حذر} (ḥadhdhara) — to warn}

\label{lesson:AR-C324-hadhdhara}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for boyhood, then the Arabic for middle age.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{حذر}}
\textbf{\ar{حذر}} — \emph{ḥadhdhara} — \textquotedblleft{}to warn\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{حذرت} \ar{الأم} \ar{ابنها} \ar{من} \ar{النار}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ḥadhdharat al-umm ibnahā min an-nār.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The mother warned her son about the fire.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يحذر}, \emph{yuḥadhdhir}.

It takes \ar{من} for the danger: \ar{حذره} \ar{من} \ar{البرد}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{حذر}} (\emph{ḥadhdhara}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḥ-dh-r} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to be wary, on one's guard\textquotedblright{}; \emph{ḥadhar} is caution. It is Form II, \textquotedblleft{}to put someone on guard\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḥadhdhara}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḥadhdhara}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḥadhdharat al-umm ibnahā min an-nār.} — The mother warned her son about the fire.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for boyhood, then the Arabic for middle age, then say \emph{ḥadhdhara} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{حذر} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To warn\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{هدد} (haddada)}{هدد (haddada)}]{\ar{هدد} (haddada) — to threaten}

\label{lesson:AR-C324-haddada-threaten}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for middle age, then the Arabic for to warn.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{هدد}}
\textbf{\ar{هدد}} — \emph{haddada} — \textquotedblleft{}to threaten\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{هدد} \ar{الرجل} \ar{جاره} \ar{بالشرطة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{haddada ar-rajul jārahu bi-sh-shurṭa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The man threatened his neighbour with the police.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يهدد}, \emph{yuhaddid}.

The danger itself is \ar{تهديد}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{هدد}} (\emph{haddada}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{h-d-d} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to pull down a building\textquotedblright{}. Form II \emph{haddada}, to threaten, is usually explained as threatening with that ruin.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{haddada}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{haddada}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{haddada ar-rajul jārahu bi-sh-shurṭa.} — The man threatened his neighbour with the police.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for middle age, then the Arabic for to warn, then say \emph{haddada} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{هدد} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To threaten\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{إنذار} (indhār)}{إنذار (indhār)}]{\ar{إنذار} (indhār) — an alarm; a warning}

\label{lesson:AR-C324-indhar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to warn, then the Arabic for to threaten.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{إنذار}}
\textbf{\ar{إنذار}} — \emph{indhār} — \textquotedblleft{}an alarm; a warning\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{انطلق} \ar{إنذار} \ar{الحريق} \ar{في} \ar{المدرسة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{inṭalaqa indhār al-ḥarīq fī al-madrasa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The fire alarm went off in the school.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{إنذار}} (\emph{indhār}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{n-dh-r} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to vow; to warn\textquotedblright{}. \emph{Indhār} is the verbal noun of Form IV \emph{andhara}, \textquotedblleft{}to warn of danger\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{indhār}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{indhār}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{inṭalaqa indhār al-ḥarīq fī al-madrasa.} — The fire alarm went off in the school.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to warn, then the Arabic for to threaten, then say \emph{indhār} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{إنذار} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An alarm; a warning\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{صفارة} (ṣaffāra)}{صفارة (ṣaffāra)}]{\ar{صفارة} (ṣaffāra) — a whistle; a siren}

\label{lesson:AR-C324-saffara}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to threaten, then the Arabic for an alarm.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{صفارة}}
\textbf{\ar{صفارة}} — \emph{ṣaffāra} — \textquotedblleft{}a whistle; a siren\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{سمعنا} \ar{صفارة} \ar{سيارة} \ar{الإسعاف}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{samiʿnā ṣaffārat sayyārat al-isʿāf.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We heard the ambulance siren.
\end{quote}

\ar{صفارة} \ar{الإنذار}: an alarm siren.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{صفارة}} (\emph{ṣaffāra}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ṣ-f-r} (Lane), where \emph{ṣafara} is \textquotedblleft{}to whistle\textquotedblright{}. The \emph{faʿʿāla} pattern names a tool that does a thing again and again.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṣaffāra}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṣaffāra}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{samiʿnā ṣaffārat sayyārat al-isʿāf.} — We heard the ambulance siren.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to threaten, then the Arabic for an alarm, then say \emph{ṣaffāra} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{صفارة} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A whistle; a siren\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{فوضى} (fawḍā)}{فوضى (fawḍā)}]{\ar{فوضى} (fawḍā) — chaos, disorder}

\label{lesson:AR-C324-fawda}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for an alarm, then the Arabic for a whistle.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{فوضى}}
\textbf{\ar{فوضى}} — \emph{fawḍā} — \textquotedblleft{}chaos, disorder\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{كانت} \ar{الغرفة} \ar{في} \ar{فوضى} \ar{كبيرة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kānat al-ghurfa fī fawḍā kabīra.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The room was in a terrible mess.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{فوضى}} (\emph{fawḍā}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{f-w-ḍ} (Lane), where \emph{qawm fawḍā} is a people who are all equal, with no chief over them: everyone at once.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fawḍā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fawḍā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kānat al-ghurfa fī fawḍā kabīra.} — The room was in a terrible mess.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for an alarm, then the Arabic for a whistle, then say \emph{fawḍā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{فوضى} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Chaos, disorder\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[(dialogue)]{Words from chapters 317–324 — a review}

\label{lesson:AR-R324-review-317-324}



\begin{quote}
Say the Arabic for to seize and to detain.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item to seize, to detain, to stop someone, a patrol, a checkpoint
  \item a civilization, a trace, remains of a dwelling, a temple, a pyramid
  \item condolence, to console, to lament, to announce a death, mourning
  \item the media, an agency, a source, to give news, to clarify
  \item a robber, a pickpocket, a gang, to rob, to loot
  \item a castle, a fort, a city wall, to besiege, to defend
  \item to be reared, to be brought up, a birthplace, boyhood, middle age
  \item to warn, to threaten, an alarm, a whistle, chaos
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
To seize? (\textbf{\ar{قبض}}, \emph{qabaḍa}.) To detain? (\textbf{\ar{احتجز}}, \emph{iḥtajaza}.) To stop someone? (\textbf{\ar{أوقف}}, \emph{awqafa}.) A patrol? (\textbf{\ar{دورية}}, \emph{dawriyya}.) A checkpoint? (\textbf{\ar{حاجز}}, \emph{ḥājiz}.) A civilization? (\textbf{\ar{حضارة}}, \emph{ḥaḍāra}.) A trace? (\textbf{\ar{أثر}}, \emph{athar}.) Remains of a dwelling? (\textbf{\ar{أطلال}}, \emph{aṭlāl}.) A temple? (\textbf{\ar{معبد}}, \emph{maʿbad}.) A pyramid? (\textbf{\ar{هرم}}, \emph{haram}.) Condolence? (\textbf{\ar{عزاء}}, \emph{ʿazāʾ}.) To console? (\textbf{\ar{عزى}}, \emph{ʿazzā}.) To lament? (\textbf{\ar{رثى}}, \emph{rathā}.) To announce a death? (\textbf{\ar{نعى}}, \emph{naʿā}.) Mourning? (\textbf{\ar{حداد}}, \emph{ḥidād}.) The media? (\textbf{\ar{إعلام}}, \emph{iʿlām}.) An agency? (\textbf{\ar{وكالة}}, \emph{wakāla}.) A source? (\textbf{\ar{مصدر}}, \emph{maṣdar}.) To give news? (\textbf{\ar{أفاد}}, \emph{afāda}.) To clarify? (\textbf{\ar{أوضح}}, \emph{awḍaḥa}.) A robber? (\textbf{\ar{سارق}}, \emph{sāriq}.) A pickpocket? (\textbf{\ar{نشال}}, \emph{nashshāl}.) A gang? (\textbf{\ar{عصابة}}, \emph{ʿiṣāba}.) To rob? (\textbf{\ar{سلب}}, \emph{salaba}.) To loot? (\textbf{\ar{نهب}}, \emph{nahaba}.) A castle? (\textbf{\ar{قلعة}}, \emph{qalʿa}.) A fort? (\textbf{\ar{حصن}}, \emph{ḥiṣn}.) A city wall? (\textbf{\ar{سور}}, \emph{sūr}.) To besiege? (\textbf{\ar{حاصر}}, \emph{ḥāṣara}.) To defend? (\textbf{\ar{دافع}}, \emph{dāfaʿa}.) To be reared? (\textbf{\ar{نشأ}}, \emph{nashaʾa}.) To be brought up? (\textbf{\ar{ترعرع}}, \emph{taraʿraʿa}.) A birthplace? (\textbf{\ar{مسقط} \ar{رأس}}, \emph{masqaṭ raʾs}.) Boyhood? (\textbf{\ar{صبا}}, \emph{ṣibā}.) Middle age? (\textbf{\ar{كهولة}}, \emph{kuhūla}.) To warn? (\textbf{\ar{حذر}}, \emph{ḥadhdhara}.) To threaten? (\textbf{\ar{هدد}}, \emph{haddada}.) An alarm? (\textbf{\ar{إنذار}}, \emph{indhār}.) A whistle? (\textbf{\ar{صفارة}}, \emph{ṣaffāra}.) Chaos? (\textbf{\ar{فوضى}}, \emph{fawḍā}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
